title: Desk Guidance: Stopping a Project and What It Costs by Stage
content:
# Desk Guidance — Stopping a Project and What It Costs by Stage

General basis on which an Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects project is stopped, as the desk states it to an owner. Four former clauses are retained in quotation and marked as no longer in force; the class's stage fees and restocking fee remain values of the class.

## Rule in force

An owner may stop a project, and what it costs depends on the stage it had reached.

A project the company stops because the owner has not paid carries no cancellation fee but does carry the work performed and the remobilisation fee if it restarts.

## Former stage clauses

> Cancelled after award and before the equipment order is released, the tier's awarded-stage fee applies to the contract value.

**No longer in force**; superseded by the current basis.

> Cancelled after the equipment is released, the tier's scheduled-stage fee applies and the supplier's restocking fee is passed through on equipment that can be returned, while equipment that cannot be returned is invoiced in full and left with the owner.

**No longer in force**; superseded by the current basis.

> Cancelled after mobilisation, the tier's in-progress fee applies on top of everything earned to the stop day, and retainage already withheld is released against the final settlement.

**No longer in force**; superseded by the current basis.

> Deposits are applied to the settlement and refunded only where the settlement is smaller than the deposit.

**No longer in force**; superseded by the current basis.

## The three stages

| Stage the project had reached | What the class schedule names it |
|---|---|
| after award and before the equipment order was released | the awarded-stage fee |
| after the equipment order was released and before mobilisation | the scheduled-stage fee |
| after mobilisation | the in-progress fee |

## Points of judgement

**The company stopped the work because progress billings went unpaid, and the owner asks what cancellation fee applies.** None. A project the company stops for non-payment carries the work performed and, if it restarts, the remobilisation fee, but no cancellation fee.
